shipReasons: HOLD, and the hold is one root cause with two faces, both inside the change this release made. PR-0076: chapter 5's shipped intended strategy goes from 40 wins in 40 seeds to 0 in 40 the moment the player takes any decision time, because Active ATB now runs the clock under an open menu — reproduced independently of the builder, with the D=0 arm as its own regression control. On the previous live build the clock stood still under the menu and that line was winnable. A shipped chapter whose declared canonical clear stops being winnable at human speed is a regression against live at major severity, and RUBRIC section 3 makes that a HOLD.

PR-0080 is the same change seen from the player's seat and holds on its own terms: with no keypress between two samples the open command menu changed from Yuna's list to Rikku's in 262 ms, in place, with the cursor never moving — so the row a player is reading becomes a different girl's command under their thumb — while the guide and advisor cards were captured naming a third state. Neither is tagged inNewFeature, and the distinction matters. Active ATB did not ship alongside the old behaviour with a switch: it REPLACED Wait in both shipped FFX-2 chapters and the player cannot opt out. The rubric's new-feature exemption exists because such a feature can ship switched off; this one is the shipped behaviour.

The hold is not a judgment on the decision. Active is Bailey's explicit D-009 pick and the implementation is faithful, measured and well tested; the fidelity is right and the balance consequence is the defect. No boss was tuned and none should be (hard rule 6). The correction is player-side and is already measured: four in five lost menus are section 1.7 chain locks, so letting a chain-locked girl keep her queued command recovers most of the loss without touching Vegnagun.
